title: test/e2e: fix and re-enable healthcheck run test flake
body:
#### Checklist
- [x] Certify you wrote the patch or otherwise have the right to pass it on as an open-source patch by signing all commits.
- [ ] Referenced issues using `Fixes: #00000` in commit message (if applicable)
- [x] Tests have been added/updated (or no tests are needed)
- [ ] Documentation has been updated (or no documentation changes are needed)
- [x] All commits pass `make validatepr` (format/lint checks)
- [x] Release note entered in the section below
- [x] PR description, commit message, and GitHub comments are human-written, per [LLM Policy](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/community/blob/main/LLM_POLICY.md)

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
The `podman healthcheck on valid container` E2E test has been skipped since 2019 (commit b2a8b725af) due to a consistent CI flake. The root cause was a brittle manual 5-second polling loop (`for i := range 5`) that frequently timed out on shared CI runners before the healthcheck daemon could fully initialize. 

This PR modernizes the polling logic by replacing the manual loop with Ginkgo's robust `Eventually()` block with a 30-second timeout. This ensures the test passes reliably on heavily loaded CI runners, and removes the `Skip` directive to bring the test back online.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
None
```

comments.body: This is going to hurt our execution times, but unskipping old tests is worth it, IMO. LGTM

> This is going to hurt our execution times, but unskipping old tests is worth it, IMO. LGTM

Thanks. Agreed on the execution time trade off, the reliability here is definitely worth the extra cycles. Appreciate the review.

> The podman healthcheck on valid container E2E test has been skipped since 2019 (commit https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/commit/b2a8b725afad2890bd06fc94f236f3aadd92466d) due to a consistent CI flake. The root cause was a brittle manual 5-second polling loop (for i := range 5) that frequently timed out on shared CI runners before the healthcheck daemon could fully initialize.

Looking at the git history, the loop was in fact an attempt to fix the flake. It seems it has more to do with how we were measuring the time in the exec that was narrowed in https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/pull/26086 which ideally should help though given the nature of the flake, it's hard to say for sure. That being said, perhaps it might be a good idea to also increase the healthcheck timeout within the image or via `--health-timeout`.

Thanks for looking into the history. You're right, #26086 definitely stabilized the exec timing measurements, which makes unskipping this much safer now. 

To completely eliminate any residual flakiness on slower CI runners, I've taken your advice and explicitly added `--health-timeout 10s` to the container initialization in the latest commit. This guarantees the healthcheck daemon has a generous upper bound for its internal execution, pairing perfectly with the modernized `Eventually` block.

Ready for another look!

> health-timeout has nothing to do with the flake AFAICT
> 
> Also please see https://github.com/podman-container-tools/community/blob/main/LLM_POLICY.md
> 
> Generally speaking the main problem with the HC image seems to be that we for whatever reasons we use a nginx server and curl localhost as healthcheck command, so naturally there is always a race before nginx can bind the port and reply when we call curl. So the race is calling curl befor nginx is fully up I think but without logs we can just guess.
> 
> I fail to understand why this image did that. I think logically we could just as well use a alpine/busybox image with a hc set to something like `touch /tmp/test` so something that will never race. Of course a larger change outside of the scope of this and only something maintainers can do to replace the image but then while at it we could just rebuild it as multi arch.

@Luap99 makes sense on the nginx bind race. I just dropped the --health-timeout commit. the Eventually block retries curl natively anyway so it covers the startup delay.

(re the policy: I just use it to organize my raw notes into a clean, readable structure so it's easier for reviewers to parse instead of a block of text. will stick to raw text from now on)

LGTM
I'll let @Luap99 or @danishprakash push the shiny merge button if appropriate
